column1: # The states a runtime permission and its app op end in, for an app that
# enters the sandbox with the permission in one state, has it or the
# sandbox's items changed while it is in, and leaves. One case per line,
# the columns separated by tabs. Played on the JVM by PermissionMatrixTest
# (android/app/src/test/.../catalog/), against FakeAndroid, a model of how
# Android 15 and later keep grants, flags and uid modes; and on a device by
# scripts/check-permissions.sh, which covers Android 13 and 14 too, and on
# Android 12 and 12L the cases without settings steps (it changes flags as
# the settings do with pm set-permission-flags, which Android 13 added).
# subject     what is looked at: contacts (READ_CONTACTS and its op), camera
#             op; the approximate permission goes with it)
# before      the permission as the app enters the sandbox, with every item
#             on: granted, denied, ignored (granted, with the op set to
#             ignore by the user), and for location: always (with
#             background location), approximate (the approximate one only)
# steps       what happens while the app is in the sandbox, or - for
#             nothing. Steps are separated by "," and each is followed by
#             the helper's check, as when the system reports a change; "&"
#             joins steps run back to back, before the helper looks.
#                                    denied in the settings, as the
#                                    granted permission whose op is ignored
#                                    counts as not granted there, so
#                                    allowing it also allows the op, and
#                                    denying it changes only its flags.
#               pm:grant, pm:revoke  the same with pm, as shell and device
#                                    management tools do: the grant alone
#               set:MODE             the subject's item to a mode
#               restart:helper       the app ops helper ends, and is started
#                                    steps joined after it happen before it
#               refuse:flags         the system refuses the next change of
#               late:sync            the permission policy's sync of the ops
#                                    lands after the next change, with the
#                                    modes from before (the JVM only; a slow
#                                    Android 13 does so now and then)
# leave       how the app leaves: disable; off (the subject's item set to
#             off, the app still in the sandbox); uninstall (uninstalled,
#             installed again and the subject's permissions granted). "&"
#             before it: right after the last step, before the helper looks
# permission  the subject's permission then: granted or denied
# mode        its op's uid mode then: allow, ignore or foreground
# reads       what the app gets: yes or no; for location precise,
# where       both, or jvm for a case a device cannot be made to play
# Both sides also check the flags: the permission is marked REVOKED_COMPAT
# only while granted with its op ignored (or, revoked, if the user had
# ignored its op before), never USER_FIXED, and for location the background
# permission is marked only while granted with location not allowed.
